newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS SAVES SLAM STREAK WITH OPEN WIN OVER CHANG.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS SAVES SLAM STREAK WITH OPEN WIN OVER CHANG.

text.p: Pete Sampras saved his Grand Slam season and delivered a birthday tribute to a beloved friend on Sunday by beating longtime rival Michael Chang in straight sets to defend his U.S. Open title.

Sampras, who nearly collapsed on court during a fifth-set tiebreaker in the quarter-finals, was at the top of his game in the final in claiming a 6-1 6-4 7-6 (7-3) victory for his fourth Open crown and eighth Grand Slam championship.

The win was worth $600,000 to Sampras, who extended his streak to four successive seasons with at least one Grand Slam title on what would have been the 45th birthday of coach and mentor Tim Gullikson, who died this spring of brain cancer.
The top-seeded Sampras also retained his world number one status in fighting off the pesky second-seeded Chang, who would have leapfrogged him in the rankings with a victory.
"It definitely saved my year," said Sampras.

Chang received $300,000 for his efforts in the last final to be played on Louis Armstrong Stadium Court. Next year, a new 23,500-seat stadium will be the centrepiece of a revamped tennis complex that is costing $234 million to renovate.
Earlier, Steffi Graf also confirmed her top seeding by beating Monica Seles 7-5 6-4 to successfully defend her title in a rematch of last year's women's final.

Sampras's powerhouse serve carried him past Chang, but his groundstrokes also had their familiar zing, unlike the form he showed in his painful struggle against unseeded Spaniard Corretja in the quarters.
"I played some good matches and I played some bad matches. I got through the Corretja match but I never thought I'd be a winner," Sampras said.
Sampras said Gullikson was also on his mind.
"Today was Tim's birthday. He would've been 45 today. I was thinking about him a lot all day," he said. "I still feel his spirit. I wouldn't be here without him."

Chang and Sampras also go way back together. They first played each other 17 years ago as schoolboys in San Diego. Chang dominated their series as juniors, but now that they are professionals Sampras has taken charge.
The 25-year-old Sampras had his serve broken only once by Chang as he beat him for the ninth time in their last 10 meetings to extend his lead in their personal series to 11-7.
"I think the best part of Pete's game tonight was his serve," said Chang. "I've played Pete so many times, I'm used to it. You just go out there and try to stay positive.
"It was one of those tough days."
Sampras got off to a booming start, setting the tone with his first swing of the racket with a 125 mile-per-hour (201 kph) service winner.
Two more aces and a service winner ended the first game.
Chang failed to respond to the challenge and Sampras raced out to a 5-0 lead before Chang won his first game of the match.
Sampras finished the one-sided opening set with another booming ace.
In the second set, Chang doubled-faulted on break point in the first game to fall behind again.
But Chang clawed his way back when Sampras returned the favour by double-faulting on break point himself in the sixth game to level it at 3-3.
Sampras surged ahead again in the ninth game. From 15-40, Chang saved one break point with an ace but lost serve on the next point when he netted a backhand approach to trail 4-5.
The top seed then served out the set at 15.
"I played my best of the tournament against Michael," said Sampras. "The first two sets I played as well as I could, I got off to a great start. It really set the tone."
Chang showed his fighting spirit in the third set, matching Sampras stroke for stroke as both held serve with ease.
In the 11th game, Chang nearly turned the tide. With Sampras serving at 5-6, Chang reached set point at 30-40 with an overhand smash set up by a blistering backhand return of a second serve.
Chang, however, netted a routine forehand volley to squander his best chance and the set went to a tie-breaker.
"On the set point, I think the net was a little high," joked Chang, who won the French Open as a 17-year-old but has fallen short in three subsequent trips to Grand Slam finals.

Sampras dominated the tie-break, winning the first three points and then three more in a row from 3-2 with a string of ferocious forehand winners to reach quadruple match point at 6-2. He finished the match two points later with a service winner.
"The serve was there, everything was just clicking and those are days you just dream about, especially in a final," said Sampras. "It was one of my best matches I've played in my career."
